tested_scope: Exactly two already-durable child completion records D1 and D2 reuse the same completion_identity I while disagreeing on canonical_child_key K1 versus K2; evaluate both arrival orders under identity deduplication before canonical-key indexing and parent aggregate construction.
reconstruction_rule_tested: On first sight of completion_identity I, retain the full identity-bound record as the candidate unique completion.
On a second durable record with the same completion_identity I, compare identity-bound canonical_child_key before any canonical-key indexing.

If the canonical_child_key differs, classify conflicting_duplicate_identity, fail closed, do not populate canonical-child-key index from the conflicting pair, and do not construct the parent aggregate.
scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to identity-deduplication fail-closed behavior for exactly two durable records sharing one completion_identity and disagreeing only on canonical_child_key, tested in both arrival orders. No claim for same-key payload conflicts, exact duplicate idempotency, concurrent writers, missing keys, normalization ambiguity, parent processed-state mutation, torn/corrupt writes, more than two records, external side effects, or Phase-1 closure.
exact_next_action: Next valid invocation: after fresh authority freeze, own-state reconstruction, and persisted/read-back preflight, test exactly one adjacent duplicate-identity case where two durable child completion records reuse the same completion_identity and the same canonical_child_key but disagree on an identity-bound payload or content digest. Verify reconstruction fails closed as a conflicting duplicate identity before parent aggregate construction. Do not test concurrent writers, parent processed-state mutation, torn writes, more than two records, external side effects, or another boundary in that invocation.
